plain.text: Jesus warned against doing good deeds to be seen by others. When you give to people in need, do it quietly, and your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

When you pray, don't make a show of it or babble on with many words. Go somewhere private. Your Father knows what you need before you ask. Jesus taught them to pray: Our Father in heaven, may your name be honoured, your kingdom come and your will be done on earth as in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. If you forgive others, your Father will forgive you.
When you fast, don't look gloomy to impress people. Look normal, and only your Father will know.

Don't store up treasure on earth, where it decays or is stolen; store up treasure in heaven, because where your treasure is, your heart will be too. The eye is the lamp of the body: what you fix your eyes on fills your life with light or darkness. No one can serve two masters. You cannot serve both God and money.

So don't worry about what you will eat, drink or wear. Look at the birds: your Father feeds them. Look at the wild flowers: not even King Solomon was dressed as beautifully. You are worth much more to God. Worry cannot add a single hour to your life. Seek first God's kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you. Don't worry about tomorrow; each day has enough trouble of its own.

summary.bigIdea: Jesus teaches his followers to give, pray and fast for God rather than for show, and to trust their Father instead of worrying.
points: Do good quietly, for God and not for applause.
Seek God's kingdom first and stop worrying about tomorrow.
summary.reflection: What worry could you hand over to God today?
